reviewer_concern: C2 mature NetEaseCrowd baselines under a chronological protocol
scientific_question: How competitive is LIR-PPTD on the complete NetEaseCrowd trace against a canonical probabilistic truth-inference method and a published online label-aggregation method when all are evaluated causally without future chunks?

dataset.name: NetEaseCrowd
dataset.raw_source: official NetEaseCrowd dataset; must match FC1 dataset_audit hashes before execution

methods.definition: canonical FC1 Full with the frozen 5% hidden selector; calibration references used only by LIR-PPTD

methods.source: Yang et al., ACM TKDD, DOI 10.1145/3630102; authors public LA_onepass repository
methods.implementation_policy: pin the fetched author-repository revision and source archive hash before any primary result is produced; if environment incompatibility prevents direct execution, use a paper-faithful port of LA-onepass only, validated on author demo/synthetic fixtures, and label it as a reimplementation; do not substitute another method

chronological_protocol.unit: native taskset group; never split a taskset across chunks
chronological_protocol.sort_key: taskset maximum completeTime, then tasksetId for deterministic ties
chronological_protocol.chunk_balance: greedy contiguous partition targeting equal task counts per capability while preserving tasksets
chronological_protocol.causal_rule: for chunk j, each external baseline is run on the prefix consisting only of chunks 1..j; no future chunk annotations or truths are visible; score predictions only for non-calibration tasks in chunk j
chronological_protocol.DS_rule: fit_predict on the current causal prefix; score only the newest chunk; this allows current-chunk unsupervised joint inference but no future information
chronological_protocol.LA_onepass_rule: process the causal prefix in frozen task-completion order using its online one-pass flow; score only the newest chunk
chronological_protocol.calibration_handling_external: external DS/LA-onepass/MV may see annotation rows from calibration tasks as unlabeled crowd labels but never see their ground truth/reference; calibration tasks are excluded from evaluation for every method
chronological_protocol.LIR_rule: run the canonical chronological LIR stream once per capability and map its predictions to the same chunk/scoring partition; no refit or retuning

primary_summary: equal-capability macro Accuracy and MacroF1 over the concatenated five causal scoring chunks; also report all six capability values

uncertainty.report: paired LIR-minus-baseline Accuracy/MacroF1 deltas with percentile 95% cluster-bootstrap CIs per capability; no significance cherry-picking

official_score_policy: official NetEase aggregate baseline scores are context only and must never be compared numerically as if they used this causal protocol

decision_policy.COMPETITIVE: if LIR is not materially worse on equal-capability macro metrics and capability-level intervals are mixed/non-dominating, state competitive longitudinal performance under distinct information/privacy semantics.
decision_policy.ADVANTAGE: if LIR has higher macro metrics and broadly positive capability-level deltas, state a causal-protocol empirical advantage, without claiming universal SOTA.
decision_policy.TRADEOFF: if DS or LA-onepass is clearly stronger, do not add baselines or tune LIR; state the observed accuracy tradeoff and position LIR on evidence authorization, privacy, persistence, and replay-safe state semantics.

forbidden_after_freeze: use ground truth for DS/LA-onepass training
compare official aggregate scores as same protocol
retune baseline hyperparameters on NetEase truths
replace a baseline after seeing results
